body.objective: Add proof-carrying finite symplectic/Poisson geometry and Hamiltonian reduction above linstruct, Lie representations, invariant theory, Groebner and semialgebraic stratification. The immediate consumers are sf:program/work/classical-closed-s3-gauged-clock-gauss-structure-theorem, sf:program/work/bridge-all-m-incidence-moment-map-intersection and sf:program/work/bridge-taub-energy-sign-structural-background-theorem. The programme has many hand-derived charges and moment-map cones, but Conflux cannot yet prove that two charge fibres, stabilizer strata or reduced pairings describe the same Hamiltonian quotient.
body.stop_condition: Represent exact finite symplectic and presymplectic spaces, Poisson tensors, Hamiltonian Lie algebra actions, equivariant moment maps, constraints, null foliations and charge fibres. Compute stabilizers, isotropy representations, Marsden-Weinstein quotients for a declared algebraic/linear class, induced reduced pairings, symplectic slices, orbit-type strata and singular reduction data; integrate with polynomial invariant rings and semialgebraic real loci. Emit explicit witnesses for Hamiltonianity, equivariance, basicness and nondegeneracy/radical after reduction. Reproduce the five compact Taub moment maps and their zero fibre, the rank-one two-field clock charge cancellation with its surviving relative phase, and one Einstein/extra charge-sector pairing. Independently verify the reduced form by a separate kernel/quotient construction. Export actions, fibres, strata and quotient maps as canonical Conflux objects so it may match reductions across presentations without conflating zero charge with gauge.
body.forbid: no vanishing charge called gauge without a null-direction/basicness proof; no regular-value theorem applied at a singular stabilizer; no quotient dimension inferred only from generic rank; no ignored discrete or global gauge action; no numerical orbit sampling called a quotient; no physics-specific D or Taub formula embedded in lib/math; no presymplectic sign promoted to a quantum norm
